question.worked_solution:
If $X$ follows a discrete uniform distribution over a set $S,$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{|S|}, & x\in S \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $X∼U\{-10,-9,-8,…,10\},$ and the set $S=\{-10,-9,-8,…,10\}$ has $|S|=10-(-10)+1=21$ items. So, we have

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{21}, & x=-10,-9,-8,…,10 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

In $S,$ the items that satisfy $-3<X\le 6$ are $-2,-1,0,…,6.$ There are $6-(-2)+1=9$ of these items. Therefore,

$$
P(-3<X\le 6)=9\cdot \frac{1}{21}=\frac{3}{7}.
$$
